sections.content:
16,340 people

were counted on the census as "registered children's nurses" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Registered children's nurses provide general or acute nursing care for children and young people with chronic or acute conditions and assist medical doctors with their tasks.

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "registered children's nurses" there were more women than men (96.9% compared with 3.1%).

This means "registered children's nurses" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "health professionals".

Men made up 3.2% and women made up 96.8% of "registered children's nurses"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "registered children's nurses" included:

  • early education and childcare practitioners
  • speech and language therapists
  • school secretaries

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 30 to 34 years. Of the whole working population 12% were aged 30 to 34 years. For people working as "registered children's nurses", 15.9% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "registered children's nurses" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "registered children's nurses" included:

  • biochemists and biomedical scientists
  • brokers
  • medical radiographers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "registered children's nurses", 9.9% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (62.4% compared with 37.6%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (98.6%) than self-employed (1.4%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
